ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Spatial-Temporal Coupling on Motion Transfer in Diffusion Transformers
PROPOSAL: We propose to analyze the spatial-temporal coupling issue in 3D self-attention blocks of diffusion transformers using synthetic data generated by manipulating the weights of pre-trained diffusion transformers. We will modify the weights to simulate perfect motion consistency, and measure the decay in performance of the model when we gradually increase the spatial-temporal coupling.
CONTROLS: ablating our synthetic data generator's influence by comparing against a reinforcement learning based motion alignement baseline, verifying the test cases where motion coupling goes to 0 and to maximal.
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We predict that the model's performance will rapidly deteriorate as the spatial-temporal coupling increases, but will still exhibit some degree of residual motion consistency due to the prior learned in the pre-trained model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Leverage Domain Knowledge to Enhance Motion Alignment
PROPOSAL: We propose to use 3D keypoints estimation and tracking to enhance motion alignment in the motion transfer process, leveraging the structural insight of object movement instead of relying solely on self-supervised learning with the video ground truth. We will modify the diffusion transformer architecture to incorporate 3D keypoints as an external validation signal, guiding the motion alignment process towards more realistic and coherent motion.
CONTROLS: comparing against the baseline where we do not use structural insight (self-supervised), ablating the validation signal strength and method to understand the performance sensitivity.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We predict that the incorporation of 3D keypoints estimation and tracking will improve the coherence and realism of the motion in the transferred videos, but may introduce additional computational complexity and memory requirements due to the added external validation signal.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Large-scale Benchmarking for Motion Transfer and Text-to-Video Generation
PROPOSAL: We propose to develop a large-scale benchmarking framework for motion transfer and text-to-video generation, utilizing a diverse set of datasets with diverse attributes, such as object movements, camera motions, environmental conditions, and text prompts. The benchmark will include comprehensive metrics to evaluate the fidelity, coherence, and diversity of the generated videos, as well as metrics to evaluate the model's ability to align with the reference motion and follow the text prompts.
CONTROLS: leveraging the Large-scale Benchmarking Submissions (LiBS) platform for ease of data collection and evaluation.
COST: 200 GPU-hours (to assemble the data and train the metrics, this will contribute little compare to results, simlilarly those in paper regarding model).
PREDICTION: We predict that this benchmark will facilitate the development of more robust and versatile motion transfer and text-to-video generation models, and enable researchers and practitioners to evaluate and compare the performance of different models on a wide range of tasks and datasets.

TITLE: Leverage Domain Knowledge to Enhance Motion Alignment
PROPOSAL: We revise the proposal to evaluate the modifications in multiple motion types: object-centric (e.g., a running person), camera-centric (e.g., panning, tilting), and hybrid movements (e.g., object moving while the camera pans). We will use a pre-defined taxonomy to classify the motion types and assess the model's performance across these categories. Additionally, we will investigate the impact of varying the senstivity of the 3D keypoints external validation signal on the motion transfer performance.
CONTROLS: compare experiments with different sensitivity levels, including 0 and "self-supervised".
COST: 120 GPU-hours (for the extra exps)
PREDICTION: We predict that the model will perform relatively well on object-centric movements, but may struggle with camera-centric or hybrid movements. The sensitivity level of the external validation signal will have a significant impact on the motion transfer performance, and finding an optimal level may require tuning for different motion types.

ACTION: REVISE
NUMBER: 2
TITLE: Leverage Domain Knowledge to Enhance Motion Alignment
PROPOSAL: We revise the proposal to improve robustness by introducing uncertainty estimation for the 3D keypoints tracking, allowing the model to adjust its alignment based on the confidence of the tracking. This addition will enable the model to better handle ambiguous or partially occluded motions, which is common in real-world scenarios.
CONTROLS: compare against a baseline where uncertainty estimation is not used, and also investigate the effect of varying the confidence threshold on the motion transfer performance.
COST: 80 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We predict that incorporating uncertainty estimation will yield an improvement in motion transfer performance, particularly for challenging cases where the motion is partially occluded or ambiguous. However, the choice of confidence threshold may require careful tuning for optimal results.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Weakly-Supervised Motion Transfer via Guided Denoising
PROPOSAL: We propose a new weakly-supervised motion transfer method that leverages the pre-trained diffusion transformer's ability to denoise and learn from samples corrupted with motion noise. We will introduce a guidance term that encourages the model to preserve the reference motion pattern in the transferred video, without requiring explicit motion labels or supervision. This approach will allow us to adapt to new domains and improve motion transfer performance on unseen data.
CONTROLS: compare against a strong baseline that requires motion labels for transfer, and also investigate the effect of varying the corruption level in the motion noise.
COST: 180 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We predict that this weakly-supervised approach will show promising results on motion transfer tasks, especially when combined with other techniques like domain knowledge and uncertainty estimation. However, the quality may degrade when faced with complex and diverse motion patterns.

ACTION: REVISE
NUMBER: 3
TITLE: Large-scale Benchmarking for Motion Transfer and Text-to-Video Generation
PROPOSAL: We revise the proposal to include an evaluation of the model's ability to generalize to out-of-distribution (OOD) motion patterns, beyond those seen in the training data. To achieve this, we will create a set of synthetic videos with novel motion patterns and test the model's performance on these challenging cases. We will also investigate the effectiveness of using domain adaptation techniques to improve generalization.
CONTROLS: use a subset of videos from the benchmark to create the out-of-distribution test set, and compare against a baseline that is not trained with domain adaptation.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We predict that the model will struggle to generalize to OOD motion patterns, but domain adaptation techniques will help to improve performance. However, the effectiveness of domain adaptation may depend on the specific application and data distribution.

ACTION: REVISE
NUMBER: 4
TITLE: Weakly-Supervised Motion Transfer via Guided Denoising
PROPOSAL: We revise the proposal to incorporate an active learning component that selects the most informative samples from the video dataset to refine the model's motion transfer performance. This approach will enable the model to learn from the most relevant and challenging cases, leading to improved robustness and generalization. We will use a combination of uncertainty-based and disagreement-based methods to select the samples.
CONTROLS: compare against a passive learning baseline where the model is trained on a fixed set of samples, and also investigate the effect of varying the number of iterations and the sample selection method.
COST: 220 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We predict that active learning will lead to significant improvements in motion transfer performance, particularly for challenging cases. However, the choice of sample selection method and the number of iterations may require careful tuning to achieve optimal results.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning for Motion Transfer
PROPOSAL: We propose a neuro-symbolic reasoning framework to enhance motion transfer performance by incorporating explicit symbolic reasoning about motion patterns. The framework will consist of a neural network that represents the motion pattern and a symbolic reasoning module that generates a stable plan for motion transfer. This approach will allow the model to reason about the motion transfer process and generate more realistic and coherent results.
CONTROLS: compare against a baseline that uses only neural networks to reason about motion transfer, and also investigate the effect of varying the complexity of the symbolic reasoning module.
COST: 280 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We predict that the neuro-symbolic reasoning framework will lead to significant improvements in motion transfer performance, particularly for complex and challenging cases. However, the choice of symbolic reasoning module and the level of complexity may require careful tuning to achieve optimal results.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Generalization of Motion Transfer to Novel Camera Angles and Viewpoints
PROPOSAL: We propose to investigate the generalization of motion transfer to novel camera angles and viewpoints by incorporating a camera perspective adaptation module into the existing framework. This module will learn to adjust the motion transfer outputs to match the reference video's camera perspective, enabling the model to transfer motion to videos shot from novel viewpoints.
CONTROLS: compare against a baseline where the camera perspective adaptation module is not used, and also investigate the effect of varying the number of training examples for camera perspective adaptation.
COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We predict that incorporating camera perspective adaptation will significantly improve the model's ability to transfer motion to videos shot from novel viewpoints, but may require a large number of training examples to achieve good performance.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Simplified Spatial-Temporal Attention LoRA for Efficient Motion Transfer
PROPOSAL: Revise our previous proposal to simplify the attention mask computation by relying on a learnable spatial attention mask. This mask is learned during the spatial tuning stage and can be used to adaptively suppress spatial details while preserving temporal coherence.
   - In the spatial stage, we fine-tune temporal LoRA and the spatial attention mask simultaneously.
   - The learned spatial attention mask can be used to selectively emphasize or suppress spatial details in the 3D self-attention layers.
CONTROLS: Compare our revised approach with the original spatial-temporal attention LoRA and vanilla LoRA on the VSB100 dataset, using the same evaluation metrics as before.
COST: Estimated compute cost: 1500 GPU-hours (cache effective)
PREDICTION: We expect our revised approach to yield better motion capture performance and faster convergence than the original spatial-temporal attention LoRA, with reduced computational cost due to the simplified mask computation.

Note: This revised proposal refines the original idea by introducing a learnable spatial attention mask, which can adapt to different spatial details in the input video. This simplification reduces the computational cost and is expected to improve performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring Motion Consistency in Large-Scale Video Transfer
PROPOSAL: Investigate the effect of motion inconsistency on the performance of motion transfer using a pre-trained Diffusion Transformer. This task is challenging due to the high-dimensional nature of the video space and the importance of preserving motion details.
   - We design a motion inconsistency metric to quantify the deviation of the transferred video from the reference motion.
   - We evaluate the transferred video on the DAVIS and VSB100 datasets, and analyze how the performance varies with respect to the motion inconsistency metric.
CONTROLS: We compare our findings to the state-of-the-art motion transfer methods, which focus on preserving motion details while adapting to changes in appearance.
COST: Estimated compute cost: 3000 GPU-hours (cache effective)
PREDICTION: We predict that large motion inconsistencies will significantly degrade the performance of motion transfer, and that our approach to motion consistency will improve results compared to previous work.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Video Domain Adversarial Training for Improved Motion Transfer
PROPOSAL: Introduce a domain adversarial training approach to improve motion transfer by learning a domain-invariant representation of the video input. This is achieved by adding a domain classifier to the motion transfer network and using it to guide the learning process.
   - During training, the motion transfer network learns to transfer the motion of the reference video while the domain classifier learns to distinguish the parodies from the original videos.
   - The domain-invariant representation learned by the model allows for more robust motion transfer and generalization across different videos.
CONTROLS: We evaluate our approach on the VSB100 dataset and compare it to state-of-the-art motion transfer methods.
COST: Estimated compute cost: 2500 GPU-hours (cache effective)
PREDICTION: We predict that our domain adversarial training approach will improve the performance of motion transfer by learning a more robust and generalizable representation of the video input.

TITLE: Streaming Video Domain Adversarial Training for Improved Motion Transfer
PROPOSAL: Revise our previous proposal for video domain adversarial training to adapt to streaming scenarios, where the reference video is not available in the entire spatial or temporal domain. This involves introducing a dynamic memory component to store relevant information from the reference video while streaming, and adapting the domain adversarial training to this scenario.
   - We modify the domain classifier to incorporate a memory component that stores the output of the reference video encoder.
   - We adapt the motion transfer network to use the information stored in the memory component during streaming.
CONTROLS: We compare our revised approach to the original video domain adversarial training and evaluate both on the VSB100 dataset.
COST: Estimated compute cost: 3500 GPU-hours (cache effective)
PREDICTION: We expect our revised approach to improve motion transfer performance in streaming scenarios and to reduce the memory requirements of the model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Text-to-Video Synthesis with Motion Transfer
PROPOSAL: Introduce a text-to-video synthesis pipeline that utilizes motion transfer to generate videos that are temporally and spatially consistent with the text description. This involves using a multimodal encoder to generate motion features from the text, and then applying the motion transfer network to generate the final video.
   - We use a topic modeling approach to generate motion features from the text description.
   - We train a motion transfer network on a subset of the text-to-video dataset to learn the mappings between motion features and video frames.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach to recent text-to-video synthesis methods and evaluate both on the xvd dataset.
COST: Estimated compute cost: 4000 GPU-hours (cache effective)
PREDICTION: We predict that our approach will be effective in generating high-quality videos that are temporally and spatially consistent with the text description.

This will provide a more comprehensive understanding of the current state-of-the-art in motion transfer.
   - We compare the performance of several baseline methods on these datasets using a suite of evaluation metrics, including PSNR, SSIM, and motion transfer accuracy.
   - We identify the strengths and limitations of each baseline method and provide guidance for future research directions.
CONTROLS: We compare our revised evaluation to recent state-of-the-art methods and provide a detailed analysis of the results.
COST: Estimated compute cost: 6000 GPU-hours (cache effective)
PREDICTION: We expect our revised evaluation to provide a more comprehensive understanding of the current state-of-the-art in motion transfer and to identify key research directions for future improvements.
